title: Sensex sheds 1,484 points as banks and metals slide; Tata Steel and APL Apollo tumble
dek: The Nifty fell 1.75 per cent to 25,349.65, erasing Friday's rally, while IT shares, gold and silver rose. Markets are shut on Tuesday for Guru Nanak Jayanti.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The Sensex fell 1,483.72 points, or 1.77 per cent, to close at 82,435.99 on Monday, and the Nifty dropped 450.95 points, or 1.75 per cent, to 25,349.65, as bank and metal shares erased Friday's gains and more. The fall wiped more than ₹6 lakh crore off the market value of BSE-listed companies, according to reports.

The decline took both indices back from the nine-month highs they reached on Friday, when the Sensex closed at 83,919.71 and the Nifty at 25,800.60. Markets are closed on Tuesday for Guru Nanak Jayanti and reopen on Wednesday, 25 November.

## What moved

Banks led the fall. The Nifty Bank index lost 3.17 per cent and the Nifty Metal index 3.68 per cent, according to reports. Axis Bank fell 3.70 per cent, HDFC Bank 3.48 per cent and ICICI Bank 3.14 per cent, reversing much of Friday's bank-led rally.

Tata Steel was the biggest loser in the Nifty, down 8.48 per cent, after it told the stock exchanges on Sunday that it would sell its tubes business and its colour-coated steel unit, Tata Steel Colors, to APL Apollo Tubes for up to ₹28,000 crore. APL Apollo's own shares fell 21.92 per cent, the steepest drop in the Nifty Midcap 100. Hindalco Industries fell 3.14 per cent.

Information technology shares went the other way. The Nifty IT index rose 1.69 per cent, with Tata Consultancy Services up 3.24 per cent, Tech Mahindra up 2.10 per cent and HCL Technologies up 1.64 per cent. Shriram Finance and Titan were also among the gainers.

Smaller companies fell less than the leaders: the Nifty Midcap 100 lost 1.01 per cent to 61,403.20 and the Nifty Smallcap 100 lost 0.66 per cent to 19,314.40.

## Why

Market commentators put the fall down mainly to profit-taking in banks after their strong run, along with uncertainty in overseas markets and continuing worries about heavy spending on artificial intelligence, according to reports. On Friday Indian shares had gained while much of Asia fell, as some global investors moved money out of AI and semiconductor stocks.

Gold and silver rose sharply. On the Multi Commodity Exchange, December gold futures were up 2.50 per cent at ₹1,24,818 per 10 grams and December silver futures up 3.15 per cent at ₹1,52,473 per kg in the afternoon, according to reports. Brent crude for February delivery edged down to about $89.36 a barrel.

## Car sales cool

Separately, figures from the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA) showed that passenger-vehicle retail sales fell 7.16 per cent from a year earlier to 7,48,616 units over the 42-day festive season, even as total vehicle retail sales, including two-wheelers, rose 2.21 per cent to a record 55.25 lakh units, according to reports.

## What to watch

When trading resumes on Wednesday, investors will be watching whether the selling in banks continues, how global markets and crude prices move, and how foreign investors respond.
